levels.label: Not yet
levels.descriptor: No assumption is named.

levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: An assumption is named but it is not one the conclusion actually depends on.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: A load-bearing assumption is named and its effect on the conclusion is stated.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: A load-bearing assumption is named, tested against the scenario, and bounded.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.descriptor: The criteria are not used.

levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: Some criteria are used and others are dropped without saying why.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: Every stated criterion is applied and the result of each is reported.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: Every criterion is applied and the response says which one decided the outcome.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.descriptor: The parts of the plan contradict each other or do not add up.

levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: The plan adds up but one part is not connected to the rest.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: The plan adds up and each part is consistent with the others and with the constraint.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: The plan adds up, is internally consistent, and states what would break it first.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.descriptor: A choice is asserted with no cost acknowledged.

levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: A choice is defended but what it gives up is not named.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: The choice is defended and what it costs or forecloses is named specifically.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: The choice is defended, its cost is named, and the strongest case against it is answered.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.descriptor: The method from the earlier case is restated without being applied.

levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: The method is applied but a difference in the new case is ignored.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: The method is applied and adjusted for what is different in the new case.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: The method is applied, adjusted, and the limit of the transfer is stated.

judgment.prompt: Recommend how Octavia should handle her tax across the coming year. State what she should set aside and from what, name the figure that would change your recommendation most if it were wrong, and say what she should do differently from a filer with employment income alone.
acceptableAnswerCriteria: Recommends setting aside a share of each business payment, grounded in the 31.2% figure or in the 22% band rate plus the 14.2% contribution.
Names the figure the recommendation is most exposed to, most defensibly the $9,350 of allowable expenses, since it changes both the income tax and the contribution.
States what differs from an employment-only filer: nothing is withheld from the business income, so the $6,012.50 has to be set aside deliberately and paid in instalments.
evidenceRequirements: Cites the $10,192.50 total tax, the $6,012.50 balance, and the $1,503.13 quarterly instalment.
Refers to the 16.7% effective rate or the 31.2% set-aside share.
lookFors: The set-aside is expressed against business receipts or profit rather than against total income.
The exposed figure is identified with a reason it could be wrong.
A response noting that a bad estimate of expenses moves both charges at once is reading the structure correctly.
judgment.commonMisconception: Assuming that tax withheld from one income source covers a filer’s whole liability.

judgment.prompt: Octavia’s effective rate is 16.7% and her marginal income-tax rate is 22%. Say what each would tell her about a decision to take on $3,000 more of business work, and which she should use.
acceptableAnswerCriteria: States that the marginal figures apply: the extra $3,000 of net income would attract 22% income tax plus the 14.2% contribution, leaving about $1,914 of it.
Explains that the 16.7% effective rate describes the whole year already earned and would overstate what the extra work is worth.
evidenceRequirements: Uses the 22% band rate and the 14.2% contribution rate when valuing the extra work.
lookFors: Both charges are applied to the extra income, not just the income tax.
The response computes what is kept rather than only naming the rates.
